title: Synergistic role of thiourea additives in efficient and stable CsPbBr 3  perovskite solar cells using a one-step spin deposition technique
content: All-inorganic CsPbBr3 perovskites have sparked considerable attention in solar applications owing to their superior thermal and environmental stability when compared to hybrid perovskites. Despite this, the limited solubility of CsBr leads to uncontrolled crystallization, inadequate film coverage, and defect-rich morphologies that lower device performance, making CsPbBr3 one-step solution deposition challenging. Here, an additive engineering strategy including thiourea is given to regulate crystallization during one-step spin deposition and improve the structural and optoelectronic aspects of CsPbBr3 thin films. Thiourea is introduced as a crystallization-regulating additive to modify the precursor environment during one-step deposition. This interaction leads to compact coatings that exhibit improved surface morphology, reduced non-radiative recombination, and increased crystallinity. With improved photoluminescence intensity, longer carrier lifetime, and reduced non-radiative recombination, the modified T30 film is consistent with reduced defect-assisted non-radiative recombination. As a result, devices fabricated with this FTO/c-TiO2/m-TiO2/thiourea-assisted CsPbBr3/Spiro-OMeTAD/Au structure achieved a notable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 5.18%, which significantly exceeds the 3.25% efficiency of a pure CsPbBr3 PSC. Additionally, the improved device retained approximately 90% of its initial PCE after 15 days under ambient conditions, suggesting that thiourea has a significant function in enhancing device stability. Additionally, SCAPS-1D simulations were implemented to verify experimental observations, demonstrating good agreement between the simulated and measured photovoltaic characteristics. These results demonstrate that concentration-controlled thiourea addition provides a simple route for regulating crystallization in one-step CsPbBr3 deposition.
